answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The meadow multiplier is published, charged in orchard, and inlet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3201 identities would post 1017 proofs and burn roughly 15 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
